title: Restaurants & kitchens
_note: English for work (english-for-work run, 2026-11-02): written by hand in British English, not yet checked by a second reader. translations.en = short definition in simple English; deHint = German translation (the 'German' tab). Words that already exist in the English lexicon are refs with a job-specific example.
intro: The words for work in a restaurant, café or kitchen: equipment, cooking, taking orders, food hygiene and talking to guests and colleagues. Every word has an example sentence from a real working day in the UK.
introEasy: Do you work in a restaurant or a kitchen? Learn the words for cooking, orders and guests here.
tipps: In a busy kitchen people speak in short calls: “Behind you!”, “Hot pan!”, “Service, please!” Say them loudly and clearly.
With guests, polite questions sound friendlier: “Would you like…?”, “Can I get you…?”, “Is everything all right with your meal?”
If a guest asks about allergens and you are not sure, never guess. Say “Let me check with the kitchen” and ask the chef.
